I have been farming a long time, and with some family members working off-farm, I will keep the plan simple and dependable rather than trying anything risky. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer in before or at sowing, irrigate at the key times, and aim for a steady yield. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land with hybrid seed because I want strong yield and stability, and I will use enough fertilizer and water to support that. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and rotation, and I will keep pesticide use limited to what I expect to need under normal conditions.
